output.source_text: The main theoretical reason the vii° chord is so rarely used is that the V7 chord (Dominant 7th) contains the entire vii° diminished triad on top (e.g., G7 = G + B-D-F). Adding the root of V in the bass provides a strong root movement by descending fifth (G -> C, a perfect cadence) instead of stepwise root movement (B -> C), giving V7 superior harmonic resolution power.

note_vi: Bài 37 của nguồn Jazz Scales (YouTube), mốc 06:51-09:04. The main theoretical reason the vii° chord is so rarely used is that the V7 chord (Dominant 7th) contains the entire vii° diminished triad on top (e.g., G7 = G + B-D-F). Adding the root of V in the bass provides a strong root movement by descending fifth (G -> C, a perfect cadence) instead of stepwise root movement (B -> C), giving V7 superior harmonic resolution power. Nguồn giảng bằng tiếng Anh, câu trên giữ nguyên lời giảng. Item còn draft: chưa ai xem lại video để đối chiếu.
